checks.what: tarhuntassa vassal_start of hittites, -1280, Karaman + Mersin + 100 km round Konya. Page: 'In the early 13th century BC, Muwatalli II moved the Hittite capital from Hattusa to Tarhuntassa'; 'The city was the capital of the Hittite Empire for a time and later became a regional power in its own right'; later 'Hattusili III ... appointed Muwatalli's son Kurunta as king in Tarhuntassa'. So the land was Hittite from the start, not an independent state 1280-1268. The page gives no year (the -1280 is the dossier's own found bridge, kept unchanged) and no province ('south-central Anatolia', location unknown; proposed Konya, Turkmen-Karahoyuk near Cumra, Sirkeli Hoyuk in Cilicia, Meydancik); the spec is exactly the dossier's found/keyframe region: 187 cells, about 47,300 km2, 31.4-35.0 E, 36.1-38.7 N, the Konya plain to the Mersin coast; no wider. The ledger has no constituent type, so the vassal tint is the closest the format allows for the capital's land. Own trial (15 s): applied; one vassal relation tarhuntassa->hittites since -1280 (event data/patches/m1300-m1201.json: events/0), the dossier's -1267 vassal_start opens no second one, 187 cells at m1200 unchanged; the -1275 render shows Tarhuntassa in the Hittite vassal tint, no holes. Nothing else moves.

assyria over babylonia, -1300..-1221, no region. Page: Adad-nirari I (1305-1274 BC MC) beat Nazi-Maruttash's Kassites; 'It took place at the town of Kar Ishtar in the province of Ugarsulu'; the victory brought 'a border realignment with Assyria extending its territory into southern Mesopotamia' 'into Pilasqu, the city of Arman in Ugarsallu and Lullumu' (undated in the reign); the quotes in why match. The conflict is an artefact: Babylonia still held the cells of its carried-over -1400 shape when Assyria's -1300 keyframe (ok) claimed them, the size rule gave them to Babylonia, and Babylonia's own -1300 keyframe (ok) then dropped them to nobody (same at -1240 for Diyala/Kermanshah/Wasit). Checked with the gazetteer: Cliopatria Assyria and Babylonia overlap in 0 cells at -1300 and 0 at -1240, while Assyria -1300 against Babylonia -1400 overlaps 271 cells and Assyria -1240 against Babylonia -1300 82 cells, so the ruling can only settle cells Babylonia's own keyframes give up and cannot take land Babylonia keeps; no other conflict of the pair falls in -1300..-1221 (Babylonia's vassal years -1225..-1216 are untouched). Own trial: applied, settled 332 cell-years in 2 years (-1300, -1240; was babylonia 332, now assyria 332); snaps babylonia_-1300, babylonia_-1240 and assyria_-1220 vanish; assyria_-1300 adds 274 (kept by others 0), assyria_-1240 adds 82. The -1270 render shows the Al-Anbar/Sala ad-Din lobe Assyrian with one stray Babylonian and one nobody cell at its edge. Weak point, not a fault: the page names Pilasqu, Arman in Ugarsallu and Lullumu (east of the Tigris), not the Al-Anbar steppe (159 of the cells); those cells are Assyria's in both dossiers' accepted keyframes and nobody's otherwise.
